I couldn't stand the new transfer student—she was loud, opinionated, and challenged everything I said. Then our debate team was stranded overnight when the bus broke down. Stuck in a diner until 3 AM, we discovered we'd grown up in the same neighborhood, lost parents young, and used arguing to hide vulnerability. She was my maid of honor.

CANDIDATE A:
I immediately liked the new transfer student—we had similar interests and temperaments. Our friendship developed easily through shared activities and natural compatibility. She was my maid of honor because we'd been close from the start.

CANDIDATE B:
The union representative who'd led the strike against my management decisions and I were both hospitalized in the same small-town ER after a factory accident. Waiting together for hours while beds freed up, we talked. He'd opposed me because my efficiency measures reminded him of the layoffs that destroyed his father's career. Understanding his fear dissolved my contempt. He became my most effective collaborator on safety initiatives.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:55"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve initial conflict and misunderstanding that transform into mutual understanding and collaboration after a shared experience reveals deeper personal connections."}
